title: CA/cert store location, creation and loading
answers: Where is the mitmproxy CA stored?
How is CertStore configured when options change?
body:
- Dir = `confdir` option (`mitmproxy/options.py`, default `CONF_DIR="~/.mitmproxy"`), basename `CONF_BASENAME="mitmproxy"`. `key_size` option (`KEY_SIZE`) and `cert_passphrase` also feed it.
- `tlsconfig.py:TlsConfig.configure` rebuilds `self.certstore = certs.CertStore.from_store(path, basename, key_size, passphrase)` when `certs`/`confdir`/`key_size`/`cert_passphrase` updated (also called from `running`); warns if `default_ca.has_expired()`.
- `certs.py:CertStore.from_store`: if `<basename>-ca.pem` missing → `create_store` (uses `create_ca`) → then `from_files`.
- `create_store` writes: `-ca.pem` (key+cert, written under `umask_secret()`; the one loaded), `-ca.p12`, `-ca-cert.pem`, `-ca-cert.cer` (Android), `-ca-cert.p12`, `-dhparam.pem` (static `DEFAULT_DHPARAM`).
- `create_ca`: RSA key exp 65537, subject==issuer (CN + O), validity now-2d..+`CA_EXPIRY` (10y), BasicConstraints ca=True critical, KeyUsage key_cert_sign+crl_sign critical, EKU SERVER_AUTH, SKI, SHA-256 self-signed.
- `from_files` loads key via `load_pem_private_key`, first cert = `default_ca`, multi-cert file → `default_chain_file`, builds `dummy_crl`.
